prompt: Does the intent attempt ONE act or SEVERAL? An act is an EFFECT on something: wearing a thing down, restoring or sharpening it, revealing what is true of it by examining it, concealing something, exposing something hidden, making a noise, opening or closing a way out, going out through one, taking or handing over a thing, or moving a person. Moving her own body from one part of the room to another is NOT an act: the room is one place and nothing records where in it she stands, so walking over to a thing, stepping back, turning, or standing somewhere is never counted. But CHANGING HER POSTURE is an act on her own posture, like any other: going from on her feet to seated, kneeling, crouching or lying on the floor, or rising from one of those to her feet. Standing or leaning while already on her feet changes nothing and is not counted. A clause that says HOW an act is done is not a separate act: "with my hand hidden by my body", "keeping the motion small", "while talking to her". A clause with its own ACTIVE VERB is: "use my body to shield the motion", "rock the tile with my knee". Examining is ONE act however many details are looked for; a tool used on something is one act; hiding a thing somewhere is one act on the thing, and the place is only where it goes; picking a thing up in order to act on that same thing is part of that act. Speaking, watching and waiting are not acts. Answer several when two or more acts survive those rules, one when a single act does. Cite the exact words in the actor's intent that show the second act, or, for one, the words that describe the act.
